flashcards.q: Two compute pricing models and their rates?
flashcards.a: On-demand: $6.25/TiB scanned (first 1 TiB/month free, min 10MB/table, LIMIT does not reduce scan). Capacity/Editions per slot-hour PAYG: Standard $0.04, Enterprise $0.06, Enterprise Plus $0.10; commitments cut Enterprise to ~$0.054/1yr, ~$0.048/3yr; reservations start at 100 slots.

flashcards.q: The defensible on-demand vs Editions crossover method?
flashcards.a: Compute GiB scanned per slot-hour from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS (total_bytes_processed / total_slot_ms). On-demand = $0.0061/GiB; Enterprise PAYG breaks even at ~9.8 GiB/slot-hour. Above that ratio capacity wins; below it on-demand wins regardless of monthly totals.

flashcards.q: Why doesn't LIMIT reduce cost? What does reduce it?
flashcards.a: Meter counts columnar bytes read to process the query; LIMIT applies after reading. Reducers: partition pruning, clustering order matching filters, explicit column selection, materialized views, maximum_bytes_billed caps, dry-run before execute, 24h result cache for identical queries.

Active logical ~$0.02-0.023/GiB-month, automatically dropping to long-term rate (~half) after 90 days unmodified. Physical-storage billing is cheaper only if compression beats ~1.74:1 (~), and then time-travel bytes bill too.

At-least-once: ack deadline 10-600s with lease extension, exponential retry backoff, dead-letter topics after 5-100 attempts (best-effort forwarding). Retention up to 7 days enables seek/replay. Duplicates are normal - design idempotent consumers.

Pub/Sub service agent needs roles/pubsub.publisher on the dead-letter topic; without it, poison messages never forward and clog the subscription forever. Grant service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com.

flashcards.q: What do ordering keys guarantee and cost?
flashcards.a: FIFO per key only. Costs: reduced publish availability, higher latency, stuck message blocks its key's tail, push allows one outstanding message per key. Keep keys per-entity narrow; do NOT enable them under Dataflow (Beam has its own ordering via watermarks).

Pull subscriptions only, locational (single-region) endpoints, ack confirmations per message, no redelivery after successful ack. With ordering enabled throughput drops to thousands of messages/sec (~). Does NOT make external side effects idempotent.

Event-time windows, watermarks (completeness estimates), triggers (when results emit: early/on-time/late panes), allowed lateness (how long late data updates state). Exactly-once via checkpointed offsets + idempotent sinks. Classic failures: watermark lag from hot keys or source stalls, dropped late data.

flashcards.q: Ephemeral vs persistent clusters vs Serverless?
flashcards.a: Scheduled jobs -> ephemeral clusters (create/run/delete) or Serverless batches (no cluster object, per-DPU-second billing ~); interactive notebooks -> small persistent autoscaled cluster is the defensible exception. Persistent-for-batch is almost always idle waste.

flashcards.q: Looker vs Looker Studio in one line each?
flashcards.a: Looker: LookML semantic layer compiling governed metric definitions into SQL + API - bought for governance/consistency at scale. Looker Studio: free dashboarding without semantic layer. Without metric-drift problems, Looker is expensive ceremony.

Storage Write API: gRPC-based, cheaper than legacy streaming inserts (~$0.01/200MB), exactly-once append semantics via default streams, pending streams for two-phase commits. Legacy streaming inserts still work but new designs should standardize on Write API.
